title: Generation of ESC-derived Mouse Airway Epithelial Cells Using Decellularized Lung Scaffolds
protocol: Euthanize adult Wistar rats using CO2 chamber.
Observe animal for unconsciousness after approximately 2-3 minutes of CO2 exposure.
Check fill rate and chamber seal if unconsciousness does not occur within this time period.
Maintain CO2 filling for 1-2 minutes following unconsciousness.
Remove the animal from the chamber upon observing faded eye color and lack of respiration.
Secure the animal to the dissecting surface by fixing forepaws and hind legs.
Spray down the chest and abdomen area with 70% ethanol.
Access the heart and lungs by opening the thoracic cavity using a vertical incision along the sternum.
Make small incisions through the diaphragm to cause lung retraction.
Ligate the inferior vena cava with a suture.
Place a small incision in the left atrium with small dissecting scissors.
Prepare a 10 ml syringe filled with heparinized Hank’s balanced salt solution (HBSS) containing 10 U/ml heparin.
Insert the needle into the right ventricle to initiate lung perfusion at a rate of 2 ml/min.
Continue perfusion until lungs turn white and fluid from left atrium runs clear.
Expose and cannulate trachea near thyroid cartilage with a plastic catheter, securing it in place with sutures.
Setup a gravity perfusion system using a retort stand and clamp for syringe attachment.
Secure the maximum filling point of the syringe at 20 cm above lung level.
Attach a two-way stopcock to the syringe end and connect a long plastic tubing to the other end.
Pour decellularization solution into the syringe, allowing it to fill attached tubing and catheter.
Lavage lungs by filling to total lung capacity (approximately 12 ml) for 1 min, then remove catheter to allow fluid outflow.
Repeat lavage of lungs eight times with decellularization solution.
Conduct ten rinses with phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dissect the trachea and lungs free from the neck and chest cavity.
Remove the tissue and keep it in cold PBS at 4 °C until preparation for vibratome sectioning.
Prepare approximately 15 ml of 2% (w/v) agarose.
Prepare enough 6% (w/v) agarose for embedding all lobes into small rectangular blocks.
Dissolve low melting point agarose powder in PBS by microwaving.
Transfer the agarose to 50 ml tubes on a heat block and maintain temperature above 40 °C.
Dissect decellularized lung at the end of each lobar bronchus to detach each lobe using small scissors.
Pat dry each lobe using absorbent sheets to remove excess PBS.
Place each lobe inside 2% (w/v) agarose while on the heating block.
Remove each lobe after 5 min of coating in agarose and place it in a Petri dish.
Allow the surface to gel for 1 min on a cold plate.
Gently place lobes back into 4% (w/v) agarose, cool after 5 min.
Repeat coating once more with the 6% (w/v) agarose.
After sequential coating of each lobe, embed each lobe separately in 6% (w/v) agarose using metal base molds.
Ensure at least 3 mm of agarose surrounds the tissue from the edges.
Orient each lobe using forceps by positioning the largest flat edge at the surface of the metal mold facing the experimenter.
Allow blocks to gel on cold plate for at least 30 min prior to sectioning with vibratome.
Store blocks in a humidified chamber for up to 12 hr at 4 °C prior to vibratome sectioning.
Setup the vibratome by filling the sectioning chamber with cold PBS.
Maintain cold temperature throughout sectioning with the surrounding ice bath.
Remove blocks from metal molds and use a razor blade to trim down excess agarose surrounding lobes, while keeping approximately 3 mm from the edge of the tissue.
Fix tissue to the center of specimen plate using adhesive.
Submerge plate into the PBS-filled sectioning chamber.
Setup sectioning boundaries on vibratome by selecting the following speed, amplitude, and thickness values respectively: 0.2 mm/sec, 1.85 mm, and 350 µm.
Section each lobe completely.
Manually cut sections free using small scissors if a section is not fully separated by blade at the end of the section sequence.
Collect scaffold sections gently and keep in PBS on ice until the next step.
Transfer scaffold sections from PBS to microcentrifuge tubes (up to 30 sections/tube).
Treat scaffold sections with nuclease (90 U/ml in PBS) for 12 - 24 hours at room temperature on a rotator.
Transfer treated scaffold sections using forceps to new microcentrifuge tubes under sterile conditions.
Treat scaffold sections with antimicrobial solution (200 U/ml penicillin streptomycin and 25 µg/ml amphotericin B in PBS) for 6 hours at room temperature on a rotator.
Store scaffolds in antimicrobial solution for up to one week at 4°C before use.
Rinse scaffolds twice with PBS under sterile conditions after storage or treatment.
Transfer rinsed scaffolds to serum-free differentiation media (SFDM).
Maintain mouse ESC lines under feeder-free, serum-free culture using 2i conditions.
Remove cells from adherent pluripotent culture by trypsinization.
Resuspend cells in SFDM and seed at a density of 20,000 cells/ml in low-adherent plates for three days without media change to allow EB formation.
Gently transfer the EBs into 50 ml conical tubes using a 10 ml pipette after three days.
Allow EBs to collect at the bottom of the tube for 3 minutes at room temperature.
Aspirate media from EBs and add fresh SFDM supplemented with 50 ng/ml activin A.
Seed cells back onto low adherent plates at a 1:2 density.
Culture for three additional days to achieve definitive endoderm differentiation.
Collect day 6 EBs and dissociate with trypsin.
Label cells for c-KIT and CXCR4 expression using conjugated fluorescent antibodies.
Sort labeled cells using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) for both markers.
Count sorted cells using a hemocytometer.
Spin down the sorted cells at 400 x g for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in SFDM to obtain approximately 100,000 cells/10 µl/scaffold.
Transfer decellularized scaffold sections from SFDM onto hydrophobic floating membrane using sterile forceps.
Ensure scaffold sections are spread evenly on the membrane.
Prepare 6- or 12-well plates by filling wells with 1 or 0.5 ml of SFDM, respectively.
Gently place membranes into wells to allow them to float on top of media.
Pipette 10 µl of cell suspension directly onto each prepared scaffold section.
Replace SFDM media in cultures every 48 hours.
Aspirate the old media by holding the plate at a slight incline to avoid disrupting the culture.
Slowly add fresh SFDM to the culture along the side of the well to prevent sinking of floating membrane.
Maintain air-liquid cultures for up to 21 days to achieve differentiation of seeded cells into mature airway epithelia.
